problem: Audio large language models lack fine-grained spatial reasoning ability, relying on coarse binaural cues that limit accuracy in direction and distance estimation.
approach: The paper introduces SAGE, a geometry-aware audio encoder that aligns binaural acoustic features with 3D spatial structure using panoramic depth images and room-impulse responses at training time, then integrates it into OWL, an ALLM with spatially grounded chain-of-thought reasoning over direction-of-arrival and distance estimates.
contribution: OWL reduces mean direction-of-arrival error by 11 degrees and achieves o'clock-level azimuth estimation while supporting multi-step spatial reasoning.

problem: Existing mathematical reasoning benchmarks are limited in scale, language coverage, and task diversity, leaving mathematical retrieval and retrieval-augmented generation underexplored.
approach: MathNet provides 17,512 expert-authored Olympiad-level problems spanning 40 countries and 10 languages, supporting three tasks: mathematical comprehension, mathematical retrieval with 39K equivalence pairs, and Math RAG evaluation.
contribution: MathNet is the largest high-quality Olympiad dataset with the first retrieval benchmark for problem equivalence; state-of-the-art reasoning models achieve 76.8% (GPT-5) and 46.8% (Claude 4.5 Opus), showing significant remaining challenges.

problem: Automated alpha mining in quantitative finance is hindered by reward sparsity, inadequate sequential representations of formulas, and the inability to generate diverse portfolios of non-correlated alphas.
approach: AlphaSAGE combines a structure-aware encoder using Relational Graph Convolutional Networks with Generative Flow Networks and a dense multi-faceted reward structure to mine alphas via a novel generative flow network framework.
contribution: AlphaSAGE outperforms existing baselines in mining more diverse, novel, and highly predictive alpha portfolios, establishing a new paradigm for automated alpha mining.

problem: Predictive training using Koopman operator theory to accelerate SGD suffers from gradient explosion, especially for complex network structures.
approach: Predictive Differential Training (PDT) incorporates differential learning with an effective masking strategy based on dynamic consistency analysis to select high-fidelity weight predictions, and uses an acceleration scheduler to adjust prediction intervals.
contribution: PDT integrates seamlessly with existing optimizers (SGD, Adam, RMSprop, LAMB) and shows consistent performance improvement with reduced gradient explosion.

problem: The interaction between structured compressibility and adversarial robustness is poorly understood, hindering the design of models that are both efficient and robust.
approach: A principled framework analyzes how neuron-level sparsity and spectral compressibility affect robustness by examining their effects on learned representations and sensitivity directions.
contribution: The analysis reveals that compressibility induces sensitive directions exploitable by adversaries, with robustness bounds showing how compressibility impacts l-infinity and l-2 robustness; vulnerabilities persist under adversarial training and transfer learning.

problem: Exploiting symmetries in Bayesian Optimization is limited because the max kernel, which captures maximum similarity across group orbits, is not positive semidefinite.
approach: The paper revisits the max kernel idea by using a positive semidefinite projection of the max kernel to capture symmetries in expensive black-box function optimization.
contribution: The projected max kernel achieves significantly lower regret on synthetic and real-world BO benchmarks without increasing computational complexity compared to existing invariant and non-invariant kernels.

problem: Existing multimodal masked diffusion models support only simple image-level understanding and low-resolution generation, lacking unified capabilities for grounding, editing, and high-resolution synthesis.
approach: Lavida-O introduces Elastic Mixture-of-Transformers architecture that couples lightweight generation and larger understanding branches with token compression, universal text conditioning, and stratified sampling for efficient multimodal understanding and generation.
contribution: Lavida-O achieves state-of-the-art performance on RefCOCO grounding, GenEval text-to-image, and ImgEdit benchmarks while supporting 1024px synthesis and outperforming Qwen2.5-VL and Flux models with considerable speedup.

problem: Understanding how data geometry controls implicit bias and generalization in overparameterized neural networks trained below the edge of stability remains theoretically unclear.
approach: Theoretical analysis for two-layer ReLU networks examines how data geometry affects generalization through intrinsic dimension adaptation and concentration of probability mass toward the unit sphere.
contribution: For data on low-dimensional balls, generalization bounds adapt to intrinsic dimension; for isotropic distributions, mass concentration toward the sphere leads to memorization while dispersed mass enables learning shared patterns.

problem: Scaling laws and compute-optimal performance of signSGD under realistic data distributions with power-law feature and target decay are not well understood.
approach: Analysis of signSGD under power-law random features model characterizes population risk as a function of model size, training steps, and learning rate, identifying drift-normalization and noise-reshaping effects unique to signSGD.
contribution: signSGD can achieve steeper compute-optimal slopes than SGD in noise-dominant regimes, and the warmup-stable-decay schedule further reduces noise and sharpens the optimal slope.

problem: Current search-augmented language models struggle with fact-seeking questions where web search yields conflicting, noisy, or unhelpful results, especially in long-context reasoning.
approach: SealQA provides a three-flavor benchmark (SEAL-0 for near-zero accuracy questions, SEAL-HARD for challenging cases, LongSeal for long-context multi-document reasoning) to evaluate reasoning and factual accuracy with conflicting web results.
contribution: Even frontier reasoning models like GPT-5 achieve only 43.2% on SEAL-0, and test-time compute increases often plateau or decline; models struggle with document selection in long-context scenarios.

problem: The data processing inequality suggests no benefit to low-level preprocessing before classification, yet practitioners routinely perform enhancement and encoding steps.
approach: Theoretical analysis of binary classification with classifiers converging to Bayes optimal as training samples increase examines when low-level processing improves accuracy.
contribution: For finite training samples, preprocessing always exists that improves classification accuracy; the gain depends on class separation, training set size, and class balance, consistent with empirical observations on benchmark datasets.

problem: Concept Bottleneck Models enable interpretable predictions and test-time intervention on concepts, but interventions fail when the model exhibits systemic misalignment with expert reasoning due to data bias.
approach: CBDebug introduces a two-step Removal and Retraining framework where experts identify undesired concepts and the system converts concept-level feedback into sample-level auxiliary labels for supervised bias mitigation and targeted augmentation.
contribution: CBDebug significantly outperforms prior retraining methods across PIP-Net and Post-hoc CBM architectures on datasets with known spurious correlations.

problem: Training expressive flow-based policies with off-policy reinforcement learning is unstable due to gradient pathologies in multi-step action sampling, analogous to RNN vanishing/exploding gradients.
approach: SAC Flow reparameterizes velocity networks using gated and decoded variants inspired by modern sequential models, enabling end-to-end training of flow policies via noise-augmented rollouts.
contribution: SAC Flow achieves state-of-the-art performance on continuous control and robotic manipulation benchmarks while eliminating the need for policy distillation or surrogate objectives.

problem: MIP solvers generate thousands of cuts consuming gigabytes of memory while providing minimal benefit, making traditional approaches computationally expensive and memory-intensive.
approach: MIRACLE uses reinforcement learning with PPO to learn a cut-selection policy via curriculum learning and imitation learning on expert solver decisions, enabling adaptive inference with dynamic computational budgets.
contribution: MIRACLE achieves 98.1% memory reduction with 0.08% objective gap, 3.78x average speedup on MIPLIB problems, and 100% success rate on instances where SCIP fails 47-53% of the time.

problem: Text-to-motion models trained on generic text corpora lack explicit alignment between motion-related words and skeletal movements, limiting fine-grained motion understanding.
approach: Motion-Aligned Text Encoding (MATE) incorporates motion semantics into LLM word embeddings through motion localization (soft attention guidance between sub-texts and motion segments) and motion disentanglement (contrastive kinematic prototypes).
contribution: LLMs enhanced with MATE significantly surpass state-of-the-art T2M performance on two benchmarks when integrated into existing methods with minimal modifications.

problem: RL controllers struggle to satisfy trajectory-level safety and reliability constraints; formal specifications like LTL offer correct-by-construction objectives but produce sparse rewards.
approach: The paper integrates LTL with differentiable simulators by relaxing discrete automaton transitions via soft state labeling to produce differentiable rewards, enabling gradient-based learning directly from formal specifications.
contribution: The framework preserves objective soundness while achieving up to twice the returns of discrete baselines on complex nonlinear contact-rich continuous-control tasks.

problem: Existing Process Reward Models struggle with table-specific operations like sub-table retrieval and schema interaction, limiting performance in tabular reasoning for test-time scaling.
approach: TaTToo integrates tool-based verification with a dual-stage paradigm combining supervised fine-tuning on step-level annotations with reinforcement learning using tool-grounded reward shaping.
contribution: TaTToo improves downstream LRMs by 30.9% on five tabular reasoning benchmarks covering numerical reasoning, fact-checking, and data analysis.

problem: Existing methods fail to capture the complex physics of extreme collisions, producing non-physical artifacts and material adhesion at fracture interfaces.
approach: Fracture-GS enhances Collision Material Point Method with momentum-conserving interface forces and integrates it with fracture-aware 3D Gaussian continuum representation through implicit reconstruction, collision resolution, and dynamic fracture tracking.
contribution: The framework demonstrates superior physical accuracy and computational efficiency in handling homogeneous materials, heterogeneous composites, and multi-body collisions compared to existing methods.

problem: Existing protein function prediction models lack fine-grained intra-protein understanding of critical structural and functional features.
approach: VenusX is a benchmark with 878,000 samples from InterPro, BioLiP, and SAbDab covering six annotation types: residue-level binary classification, fragment-level multi-class classification, and pairwise functional similarity for active sites, binding sites, conserved sites, motifs, domains, and epitopes.
contribution: Comprehensive evaluation of diverse models (protein language models, sequence-structure hybrids, structure-based, alignment-based) reveals performance gaps across in-distribution and out-of-distribution scenarios.

problem: Generating counterfactual explanations that are robust to input and model perturbations while maintaining plausibility and diversity remains challenging in a unified, model-agnostic manner.
approach: LAPACE uses Label-conditional Gaussian Mixture VAE to learn structured latent space with class-specific Gaussian components and generates counterfactual paths by interpolating from input latents to learned centroids.
contribution: The method ensures robustness to input changes as paths converge to fixed centroids, provides diverse recourse options, and supports user-specified actionability constraints via gradient optimization.

problem: Open-set graph anomaly detection with limited labeled normal and abnormal nodes is challenging due to data scarcity for unseen anomalies and label scarcity for training.
approach: DEMO adaptively fuses multiple seen nodes to simulate unseen anomalies while dynamically adjusting sample weights based on energy gradients to prioritize informative nodes and maintain a memory bank for pseudo-labeling.
contribution: DEMO outperforms baselines on various benchmarks for detecting unseen anomalies different from training anomalies.

problem: Scaling Vision-Language Models in multi-agent systems is economically unsustainable due to high coordination costs under information asymmetry and heuristic proxies that ignore costs.
approach: Agora reframes coordination as a decentralized market for uncertainty, formalizing epistemic uncertainty as a tradable asset with market-aware Thompson Sampling extended as broker to guide cost-efficient equilibria.
contribution: Agora achieves +8.5% accuracy over baselines on MMMU while reducing cost by over 3x across five multimodal benchmarks (MMMU, MMBench, MathVision, InfoVQA, CC-OCR).

problem: Existing resting-state fMRI models trained on limited data struggle to generalize across diverse populations and scanning protocols.
approach: MnemoDyn uses a dynamical-systems based model with multi-resolution temporal modeling on 40K rs-fMRI sequences across public and permission-based datasets, trained without transformer backbones.
contribution: MnemoDyn delivers superior reconstruction quality compared to state-of-the-art transformer-based approaches and generalizes well across populations and protocols while being compute efficient.

problem: RAG systems expose external knowledge bases to extraction attacks via malicious inputs, but detection is easy; extraction via benign queries remains understudied.
approach: IKEA uses anchor concepts (knowledge-related keywords) to generate natural queries, then applies Experience Reflection Sampling and Trust Region Directed Mutation to exhaustively explore RAG's embedding space.
contribution: IKEA surpasses baselines by over 80% in extraction efficiency and 90% in attack success rate; substitute RAG systems built from IKEA extractions show close performance to originals.

problem: World models for autonomous driving suffer from identity drift, where objects change appearance or category across frames due to lack of instance-level temporal constraints.
approach: ConsisDrive introduces Instance-Masked Attention and Instance-Masked Loss to enforce temporal consistency at the instance level, ensuring visual tokens interact only with corresponding instance features.
contribution: ConsisDrive achieves state-of-the-art driving video generation quality and demonstrates significant improvements in downstream autonomous driving tasks on nuScenes.

problem: Discrete Level-of-Detail rendering requires significant storage for model copies and causes jarring visual popping artifacts during transitions.
approach: CLoD-GS introduces a continuous LoD mechanism directly into 3D Gaussian Splatting with learnable distance-dependent decay parameters that adjust Gaussian opacity based on viewpoint proximity.
contribution: CLoD-GS enables smooth quality scaling within a single unified model while reducing primitive count and memory footprint compared to discrete methods.

problem: Traditional CFD and graphics pipelines for fire effects require handcrafted geometry and expert-tuned parameters, limiting scalability to real-world scenes.
approach: FieryGS integrates multimodal LLM-based material reasoning, efficient volumetric combustion simulation, and unified rendering of fire and 3DGS through three modules: implicit reconstruction, combustion simulation, and dynamic fracture tracking.
contribution: FieryGS enables realistic, controllable fire synthesis in real scenes with precise user control over intensity, airflow, ignition location, and other combustion parameters.

problem: Standard preference elicitation methods fail to capture true cognitive processes behind human decision-making, such as use of heuristics and simplifying thought patterns.
approach: An axiomatic approach learns cognitively faithful decision processes from pairwise comparisons where features are processed with learned rules then aggregated via fixed rules like Bradley-Terry.
contribution: The method learns interpretable models of human decision-making in kidney allocation tasks matching or surpassing prior accuracy on pairwise decision-making.

problem: Existing machine-generated text detectors struggle to identify task-specific MGT on real-world platforms like Wikipedia, where tasks like summarization produce text resembling human writing.
approach: TSM-Bench provides a multilingual, multi-generator, multi-task benchmark for evaluating MGT detectors on common Wikipedia editing tasks, revealing generalization asymmetries.
contribution: Average detection accuracy drops 10-40% compared to prior benchmarks; fine-tuning on task-specific data enables cross-domain generalization but not vice versa.

problem: Cascaded speech systems transcribe and resynthesize, discarding paralinguistic cues and creating a text bottleneck; text-guided systems still rely on text intermediates.
approach: A true speech-to-speech LLM uses modality-based layer-splitting architecture with frozen pre-training to preserve reasoning while adding native speech capabilities without text guidance.
contribution: The model achieves state-of-the-art spoken question answering and comparable speech-to-speech performance relative to text-guided systems while maintaining competitive text performance.

problem: Academic rebuttal is a complex strategic communication task under information asymmetry requiring perspective-taking, but current approaches miss this and imitate surface-level linguistics.
approach: RebuttalAgent grounds rebuttal in Theory of Mind (ToM) via ToM-Strategy-Response framework, trained with supervised fine-tuning on synthetic RebuttalBench (9,533 trajectories) followed by RL with self-reward.
contribution: RebuttalAgent significantly outperforms the base model by 18.3% average; Rebuttal-RM specialized evaluator achieves scoring consistency with human preferences surpassing GPT-4.1.

problem: Diffusion LLMs recompute all QKV at every denoising step and layer despite minimal KV state changes, creating substantial redundancy and high decoding latency.
approach: Elastic-Cache performs adaptive layer-aware KV cache updates by deciding when to refresh via attention-aware drift test on most-attended tokens and where via depth-aware schedule.
contribution: Elastic-Cache achieves 8.7x speedup on GSM8K (256 tokens), 45.1x on longer sequences, and 4.8x on HumanEval with negligible generation quality loss.

problem: Generating short movies from textual descriptions while maintaining long-range coherence in both storyline and visual appearance is challenging.
approach: Captain Cinema uses top-down keyframe planning to generate narrative keyframes ensuring coherence, then bottom-up video synthesis conditioned on keyframes; includes interleaved training strategy for Multimodal Diffusion Transformers.
contribution: Captain Cinema demonstrates favorable performance in automated creation of visually coherent and narratively consistent short films.

problem: Explaining RL agent policies in natural language requires handling pluralistic and probabilistic human judgments about explanation quality, not captured by point estimates.
approach: The framework trains LLMs for explanation generation via RL from AI feedback using rewards from continuous normalizing flows that capture probabilistic human reward distributions.
contribution: CNF-based rewards yield explanations enabling more accurate agent decision predictions, greater logical soundness and actionability, and lower cognitive load than prior RLHF/RLAIF methods.

problem: Knowledge editing and unlearning mechanisms in LLMs remain largely unexplored due to insufficient, isolated, small-scale evaluation.
approach: KnowledgeSmith proposes a unified framework casting editing and unlearning as constrained optimization, with automatic dataset generator providing structured interventions across graph levels and data scales.
contribution: Results show LLMs do not exhibit similar updating as humans for different knowledge levels, and there exists consistency-capacity trade-off between editing reliability and model performance.

problem: LoRA fine-tuning faces generalization challenges, and applying Sharpness-Aware Minimization to LoRA is computationally expensive due to sequential QKV computation.
approach: Bi-LoRA introduces auxiliary adversarial LoRA module that decouples sharpness optimization from task adaptation, enabling parallel computation while providing perturbations outside the primary module's optimization subspace.
contribution: Bi-LoRA roughly halves SAM application time for LoRA while achieving both efficiency and effectiveness across diverse architectures and tasks.

problem: Knowledge distillation typically forces students to mimic teacher distributions over entire outputs, causing distribution mismatch especially in complex reasoning tasks with limited student capacity.
approach: Token-Selective Dual Knowledge Distillation combines indirect distillation (teacher re-ranks student-proposed responses) and direct distillation (selective token-level distribution matching based on confidence difference) with entropy regularization.
contribution: TSD-KD achieves state-of-the-art performance on 10 challenging reasoning benchmarks, outperforming baselines by up to 54.4% and runner-up by 40.3%.

problem: Computing worst-case robust real-time pursuit strategies for graph-based pursuit-evasion games under partial observability (imperfect information) is currently missing from the literature.
approach: R2PS proves dynamic programming maintains optimality under asynchronous evader moves, extends it with belief preservation for partial observability, and embeds into EPG framework for learning robust cross-graph policies.
contribution: R2PS achieves robust zero-shot generalization to unseen real-world graph structures against asynchronous-move DP evasion strategies with policy learning via RL.

problem: RL training convergence for post-training LLMs is sensitive to batching and prompt selection; optimal strategies remain unclear.
approach: Prompt Curriculum Learning uses a learned value model to select intermediate-difficulty prompts (50% model success rate) without costly rollouts, focusing on most sample-efficient prompts.
contribution: PCL achieves highest performance or significantly less training time to reach comparable performance; PCL is 12.1x and 16.9x faster at identifying intermediate-difficulty prompts on MATH and DeepScaleR.

problem: Multi-agent LLM systems lack scalable reliability due to structural fragility and the scarcity of large-scale datasets for error attribution and debugging.
approach: Aegis constructs 9,533 annotated failure trajectories via LLM-based error injection into successful executions, supporting three learning paradigms: supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and contrastive learning.
contribution: Fine-tuned LLMs achieve error attribution performance competitive with proprietary models an order of magnitude larger, validating automated data generation for reliable multi-agent systems.
